episode_row: in-place sort reordered the training frame; live model silently changed

commits.subject: fix(compute): preserve row order in hard-contact context feature
commits.body:
The hard-contact rolling block at compute.py:521 mutated df via
sort_values(["batter_id", "date"]), reordering the main dataframe for
the rest of compute_all_features. LightGBM's subsample=0.8 with
random_state=42 picks rows by index, so a reordered training frame
silently sampled different rows and produced a ~1pp P@1 regression
on the 2024 holdout (84.86% -> 83.78%) starting at 30ed4fa.

Sort a view instead. Feature values are byte-identical; only the
in-place mutation is removed. Adds a regression test that asserts
compute_all_features output is not monotone in batter_id.

Bisect: 947fce8 good -> 8224d08 good -> 30ed4fa bad -> HEAD bad
Verified three ways:
- feature-output byte equality vs pre-30ed4fa
- Mac 1-season backtest: P@1 2024 = 84.86%
- 5-season backtest on Hetzner CPX51: P@1 2024 = 84.86%
